note: The accepted residue of the recoverability invariant's widest rung (scripts/elision-monotone.ts --strict, 160 columns). Each entry is a document that still loses content at that width, with the columns it would need. The baseline MAY ONLY SHRINK: a document that no longer loses content must be dropped, and a new one fails the gate. Reshaping these is an authoring call, not a renderer one. The first two are embedded payloads whose code lines run past 200 characters — a code fence has no cap, so widening repairs them. The last two are diagrams, and they grew here on 2026-10-25 for a reason that is NOT an authoring regression: the width policy changed (BRF-DIAGRAM-WIDTH-HANDOFF, amendment) so that a diagram too wide for the glass is DRAWN AND CUT rather than REFUSED OUTRIGHT. A refused fence cut zero lines because it emitted none; a shown one cuts every line past the glass. Measured before and after on both documents: 0 art-elided lines each, now 14 and 13. The invariant the gate exists for is untouched — no document's cut count rises at a wider rung, and the corpus totals still fall monotonically with width. These two were added because a receipt is a larger loss than a marked fragment, not because the renderer got worse; the remedy for each (split the diagram, or widen) is named in playbooks/mermaid-diagrams-playbook.md. A third class joined on 2026-11-03 (the conformance plate above): the same shape as `docs/2026-10-25-test-diagrams.md` — an instrument whose width is the measurement, so reflow is the one repair that would destroy it.
